title: Laboratory Glassware, Reagents & Fume Hoods: Imperatives & Must
description: Essential English for handling beakers, pipettes, chemical reagents, and lab safety rules under the fume hood.
learning_objectives: Use simple laboratory imperatives (pour, label, store, heat)
Apply modal 'must' and 'do not' for chemical safety
Avoid basic Czech transfer in lab SOPs

questions.prompt: Always _____ the chemical reagent bottle immediately after taking a sample.
questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Vždy uzavřete lahev'. In English, direct instructions take the base verb 'Always close'.
questions.workplace_track: Hazardous Reagents, Solvent Recovery & Lab Safety

questions.prompt: You _____ pour concentrated sulfuric acid into water, never water into acid!

explanations.correct: Safety rule uses 'must' followed by bare infinitive ('must pour').
explanations.wrong_A: 'can' implies optional choice, which is dangerous.
explanations.wrong_B: 'must to' is ungrammatical (*must to* is a common Czenglish error).

questions.cz_learning_point: Never say *must to*. Use 'must + base verb': 'You must pour acid into water'.
questions.workplace_track: Hazardous Reagents, Solvent Recovery & Lab Safety

questions.prompt: Do not _____ volatile organic solvents outside the certified fume hood!

explanations.correct: Negative imperative 'Do not' requires base verb 'heat'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Nezahřívejte těkavá rozpouštědla'. Use 'Do not heat'.
questions.workplace_track: Hazardous Reagents, Solvent Recovery & Lab Safety

questions.prompt: The analytical chemist _____ the pH buffer solution before each titration test.

explanations.correct: Singular subject 'The chemist' takes 'calibrates' with third person '-s'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Chemik kalibruje'. Third person singular in English requires '-s': 'calibrates'.

questions.prompt: Where _____ the safety data sheet (SDS) for this solvent stored?

explanations.correct: Singular subject 'sheet' takes 'is' with passive participle 'stored'.
explanations.wrong_A: 'does' is auxiliary for action verbs, not passive state.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Kde je uložen bezpečnostní list?'. Singular subject takes 'Where is the sheet stored?'.
questions.workplace_track: Hazardous Reagents, Solvent Recovery & Lab Safety

questions.prompt: Lab technicians _____ wear chemical-resistant nitrile gloves when handling acetone.

explanations.correct: Modal 'must' is followed directly by bare infinitive ('must wear').

questions.cz_learning_point: Never say *must to wear*. Always use 'must wear'.
questions.workplace_track: Hazardous Reagents, Solvent Recovery & Lab Safety

questions.prompt: Please _____ every glass flask with the batch number and expiration date.

explanations.correct: 'Please' is followed by base imperative verb 'label'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Prosím označte...'. In English, use 'Please label every flask'.
questions.workplace_track: Hazardous Reagents, Solvent Recovery & Lab Safety

questions.prompt: The analytical balance in lab 3 _____ accurate to four decimal places.
questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Váha je přesná'. Singular subject $\rightarrow$ 'is accurate'.

questions.prompt: The sample solution _____ not dissolve at room temperature; it requires heating.

explanations.correct: Singular subject 'The solution' takes 'does not dissolve'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'Roztok se nerozpouští'. Say 'does not dissolve', not *is not dissolve*.

questions.prompt: All flammable waste solvents must be poured _____ the dedicated red container.

explanations.correct: 'Pour into' indicates movement into an enclosed vessel or container.
explanations.wrong_A: 'to' denotes direction toward, but liquid goes inside $\rightarrow$ 'into'.

questions.cz_learning_point: Czech 'nalít do nádoby'. English uses 'pour into the container'.
questions.workplace_track: Hazardous Reagents, Solvent Recovery & Lab Safety
